overview: The Deeds Office (under the Department of Agriculture, Land Reform and Rural Development) is responsible for registering ownership of property in South Africa. Every property transfer, bond registration, and servitude must be registered here. The Durban Deeds Office serves the KwaZulu-Natal region.

services.name: Title Deed Search
services.description: Check who owns a specific property, what bonds are registered against it, and if there are any restrictions.
how: Visit the Durban Deeds Office in person — searches are done at the public search counter
You can search by property description (erf number, township name) or by owner name
A basic search costs approximately R30 per property
You can also use the online Deeds Web portal (www.deedsweb.gov.za) — registration required, costs apply
For more detailed information, engage a conveyancing attorney
why_you_might_need_this: Buying property — confirm the seller is the registered owner
Boundary disputes — confirm exact property descriptions
Debt collection — check if a debtor owns property
Estate administration — identify deceased person's property

services.name: Property Transfer
services.description: When property changes hands (sale, donation, inheritance), the transfer must be registered at the Deeds Office.
process: A conveyancing attorney handles the transfer — this is legally required
The attorney prepares all transfer documents
Both buyer and seller sign documents at the attorney's office
The attorney lodges documents at the Deeds Office
The Deeds Office examines and registers the transfer
Processing time: approximately 2-3 weeks after lodgement
The new title deed is issued in the buyer's name
costs: Transfer duty: payable to SARS — calculated on the property value (first R1.1 million is exempt for natural persons)
Conveyancing fees: regulated by the Law Society, based on property value
Deeds Office fees: approximately R700-R2,000 depending on the transaction
Rates clearance certificate from the municipality

services.name: Bond Registration
services.description: When you take a home loan, the bank registers a mortgage bond against your property at the Deeds Office.
process: Your bank appoints a bond attorney
You sign at the attorney's office
The attorney lodges at the Deeds Office

services.name: Bond Cancellation
services.description: When you pay off your home loan in full, the bond must be cancelled at the Deeds Office.
process: Notify your bank that the loan is paid in full
The bank instructs a cancellation attorney
The attorney prepares cancellation documents and lodges at the Deeds Office
The bank should cover the cancellation attorney's fees

deeds_office_durban.address: Salmon Grove Chambers, 407 Anton Lembede Street, Durban CBD

common_problems.what_to_do: Apply for a certified copy of the title deed at the Deeds Office. You will need an affidavit confirming the loss and payment of approximately R150.

common_problems.problem: Property registered in deceased person's name
common_problems.what_to_do: The executor of the estate (appointed by the Master of the High Court) must transfer the property to the heir(s). Contact the Master's Office in Durban: 031 372 3000.

common_problems.problem: Property sold but transfer not registered
common_problems.what_to_do: Contact the conveyancing attorney who handled the sale. If the attorney is unresponsive, lodge a complaint with the Law Society of South Africa: 012 366 8800.

common_problems.problem: Suspicious activity on your title deed (someone trying to transfer without your knowledge)
common_problems.what_to_do: Register for Property Alert at the Deeds Office or online — you will be notified of any activity against your property. Report suspected fraud to SAPS immediately.

escalation.step_1: Contact the Durban Deeds Office directly: 031 334 5300
escalation.step_2: Escalate to the Chief Registrar of Deeds: 012 338 7200
escalation.step_3: Lodge a complaint with the Department of Agriculture, Land Reform and Rural Development
escalation.step_4: If an attorney is involved in wrongdoing, report to the Legal Practice Council: 012 366 8800
escalation.legislation: Deeds Registries Act 47 of 1937, Sectional Titles Act 95 of 1986

your_rights: Section 25 of the Constitution protects property rights
No one may be deprived of property except in terms of a law of general application
You have the right to search the Deeds Office records — they are public records
You have the right to a certified copy of your title deed
Property Alert service helps protect against fraudulent transfers
